idiom_name: keyed store + replacement policy + invalidation rule (no language primitive)
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: wrap the provider behind a single facade whose read path derives a canonical key, looks it up in a bounded store, and on a miss acquires the resource once and stores it with its metadata (size, last use, expiry). Keep the replacement policy (what leaves when the bound is reached), the invalidation rule (what makes an entry unusable: TTL, write-through, event-driven purge) and the access policy (admission, single-flight for concurrent misses) as separate, replaceable decisions. The provider stays authoritative and the cache stays disposable: every entry must be recomputable, and losing the whole cache must cost latency only.
code_sketch:
get(key):
    e = store.lookup(canonical(key))
    if e is valid:
        touch(e); return e.value              # hit
    value = acquire(key)                      # miss: provider call (single-flight)
    store.put(key, value, size, expiry)       # may evict per replacement policy
    return value
# writer path: commit to provider, then invalidate(key)
# bound: max_entries + max_weight; policy: LRU | LFU | TTL
pitfalls: Skip the capacity or weight bound -> the store grows until eviction pressure becomes a memory or latency outage -> enforce entry and weight limits with a policy chosen from measured access and value-size distributions.

Leave replacement implicit -> insertion order or an accidental library default evicts useful hot entries, or nothing is evicted at all -> choose and test LRU, LFU, FIFO, or weighted admission explicitly.

Invalidate only in the read facade -> bulk SQL, a direct writer, or another service leaves stale entries that look fresh -> centralize delete or update after the authoritative commit and enumerate every writer.
Give entries identical TTLs -> entries populated together expire together and stampede the provider -> add bounded jitter and single-flight, refresh-ahead, or lease protection for hot keys.

Cache transient not-found or error results forever -> a recoverable provider fault becomes a permanent false-negative -> cache negative results only with a short, explicit expiry and distinguish them from failures.
Omit tenant, authorization, locale, or representation from the key -> one caller receives another caller's value -> derive an immutable canonical key from every dimension that changes the answer.
Treat the cache as authoritative -> an eviction, restart, or invalidation wave loses business state -> keep the provider authoritative and make every cached entry recomputable.

Wrong move: add caching before measurement, as a cargo-cult default -> the invalidation surface, stale-read bugs and memory cost are paid while the real bottleneck (query plan, data model, N+1 access) stays unfixed -> instead profile first, cache only where a measured read-heavy reuse ratio exists, and keep the cache removable by configuration change rather than code deploy.

Wrong move: rely on TTL alone for user-visible correctness -> a reader misses their own write for up to the full TTL after every update -> instead invalidate explicitly on the write path and treat the TTL only as the bound on invalidation bugs, never as the freshness mechanism.

Wrong move: ship a cache with no bypass or cache-busting switch -> stale-entry bugs become invisible and unreproducible because every inspection reads the same poisoned copy -> instead provide a documented way to skip or flush the cache (query flag, admin purge, config kill-switch) so the authoritative path can always be reached.
